judged_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:66-68 — decrypted `keys` JSON is written verbatim into `prisma.credential.key` for the target app without validating its shape against the app's expected credential schema, allowing an attacker who can produce a validly AES-encrypted (or, if the encryption key is misconfigured/empty, trivially self-encrypted) blob to inject arbitrary JSON into another user's stored credential object (P2, confidence 50).

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse(...)`d and then persisted directly into `prisma.credential.key` on both update and create (`data: { key: keys }`) without any validation against an app-specific credential schema. The only checks are user/app existence and webhook secret header; there is no shape/type enforcement for `keys`, so anyone who can satisfy the secret check can write arbitrary JSON into another user’s stored credential object for that app slug.
